title: Business Requirements Document — abc Chat

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: The Hospital Management System (HMS) is designed to provide a centralized platform for managing comprehensive hospital operations. The strategic rationale for this system is to streamline the end-to-end patient journey—from registration and appointment scheduling to clinical care, laboratory/pharmacy services, and billing—while ensuring strict compliance with healthcare data privacy standards. By integrating role-based access control for diverse stakeholders (Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient), the system aims to enhance operational efficiency, improve patient care quality, and ensure the secure management of sensitive medical records and financial data.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body:
**Business Objectives:**
1. Centralize hospital operations to eliminate data silos across departments.
2. Ensure secure and compliant management of Protected Health Information (PHI).
3. Optimize resource allocation through real-time bed/ward management and inventory tracking.
4. Enhance patient experience via a self-service portal for appointments, prescriptions, and billing.

**Success Metrics:**
- **Operational Efficiency:** Reduction in manual processing time for patient registration and billing.
- **System Availability:** High availability of the platform to support continuous hospital operations.
- **Compliance:** 100% adherence to HIPAA and GDPR standards for data privacy and security.
- **User Adoption:** Successful onboarding of all defined roles (Admin, Doctor, Nurse, etc.) with role-based access enforcement.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body:
**In Scope:**
- **Patient Management:** Registration, profile management, OPD/IPD workflows, admission/discharge/transfer.
- **Clinical Operations:** Electronic Medical Records (EMR), diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes.
- **Support Services:** Laboratory test requests/reports, pharmacy prescriptions, medicine inventory, bed/ward management.
- **Financial Operations:** Billing, payments, insurance management, invoices, receipts, hospital expenses.
- **Administrative Functions:** Staff management, inventory/procurement, audit logs, reporting, and notifications.
- **User Interfaces:** Patient portal and Doctor dashboards.

**Out of Scope:**
- Specific hardware procurement details (though hardware interfaces are implied for deployment).
- Third-party insurance provider API integrations (unless specified in future phases).
- Non-medical administrative tasks unrelated to hospital operations.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body:
The system supports the following key stakeholders and governance personas, each with specific role-based access:
- **Admin:** System configuration, user management, and overall oversight.
- **Doctor:** Clinical decision-making, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes.
- **Nurse:** Nursing notes, vital signs, and patient care coordination.
- **Receptionist:** Patient registration, appointment scheduling, and queue management.
- **Pharmacist:** Pharmacy prescriptions, medicine inventory, and dispensing.
- **Lab Technician:** Laboratory test requests, processing, and report generation.
- **Accountant:** Billing, payments, insurance management, and financial reporting.
- **Patient:** Self-service access to appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history.

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: System must support patient registration and profile management.
Patient records are created and retrievable with all demographic and medical data.
System must manage appointment scheduling and queue management.
Appointments are scheduled, and queues are managed in real-time.
System must handle Outpatient and Inpatient workflows.
OPD and IPD patient flows are tracked from admission to discharge.
System must maintain EMR including diagnosis, prescriptions, and history.
EMR is accessible to authorized roles and includes all clinical data.
System must manage lab test requests and reports.
Lab requests are generated, and reports are linked to patient records.
System must handle pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory.
Prescriptions are processed, and inventory levels are updated.
System must manage billing, payments, and insurance.
Invoices are generated, payments are recorded, and insurance claims are processed.
System must enforce role-based access for all personas.
Users can only access modules and data relevant to their role.
Patients must view appointments, prescriptions, reports, and bills.
Patient portal displays all relevant data securely.
System must maintain audit logs and ensure data security.
All access and actions are logged, and data is encrypted per HIPAA standards.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body:
**Assumptions:**
- The system will be deployed in a cloud or on-premise environment with appropriate infrastructure.
- All stakeholders will be trained on the system's functionalities.
- Data migration from legacy systems (if any) will be handled separately.

**Operational Constraints:**
- **Compliance:** The system must comply with HIPAA and GDPR regulations for data privacy.
- **Performance:** The system must support fast API responses and high availability.
- **Scalability:** The architecture must scale to handle increasing patient volumes and data loads.
- **Security:** Secure authentication, password encryption, and session management are mandatory.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body:
**Compliance Frameworks:**
- **HIPAA:** Ensures the protection of PHI through encryption at rest (AES-256) and audit trail immutability.
- **GDPR:** Applies if EU patients are involved, ensuring data protection and privacy rights.
- **HL7 FHIR & DICOM:** Standards for health data exchange and medical imaging.

**Risk Mitigation:**
- **Data Breach:** Mitigated by AES-256 encryption, HTTPS, and role-based access control.
- **System Downtime:** Mitigated by high availability architecture and regular backups (RTO < 1h, RPO < 5min).
- **Non-Compliance:** Mitigated by regular audits and adherence to HIPAA/GDPR guidelines.

**NFR Benchmarks:**
- **PHI Encryption:** AES-256 at rest.
- **Audit Trail:** Immutable logs for all access and actions.
- **Recovery:** RTO < 1 hour, RPO < 5 minutes.

Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
